reconcile.connective: Defenders deny that one situation is in view: the differing animals are graded by the offerer's rank and by the kind of offence, not assigned arbitrarily to the same case.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, compiling the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, lists these texts together as conflicting, noting the law names a different required animal — bullock, ram, or female goat — for the one situation of inadvertent sin.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); contradiction catalogued at skepticsannotatedbible.com

excerpts.excerpt_text: The former case required offering a bull, a large, expensive animal. … The latter case required a lesser animal—a male goat for a lay leader or a female sheep or goat for a common person. … The distinction stresses the responsibilities of leaders.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the 'three animals for one situation' charge by grounding the differing animals in the offerer's rank, not arbitrary inconsistency — the strongest single harmonization on the row.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on Leviticus 4 (1861-75)
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this passage directly, explaining that the sin-offering ritual 'differed, with regard to the animals sacrificed... according to the position which the person presenting them happened to occupy,' and distinguishing the trespass-offering's ram from the sin-offering animals.

link.note: Live apologetic treatment covering Leviticus 4 and Numbers 15 together, explaining the animal varies by the offerer's identity and circumstance.
